title: Crimp the board lid onto a filled foil take-out pan by folding its rim down all the way round
instruction: Crimp the board lid onto the filled foil take-out pan: fold the pan's rim down flat onto the lid all the way round, so the lid stays on when the pan is carried or turned on its side. Then let go.
context: Food preparation workers (O*NET 35-2021.00): "Package take-out foods or serve food to customers." Fast food and counter workers (35-3023.00): "Wrap menu items such as sandwiches, hot entrees, and desserts for serving or for takeout." Foil pans with board lids are closed by folding the soft rim over the lid. Ability tested: folding a soft metal rim flat over a lid section by section all the way round, while the other hand keeps the lid seated and the free pan from sliding.
setup: Station table; cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Blue polyethylene cutting board 30.5 x 45.7 x 1.2 cm, fixed, centred x 31.5, y 0, long side along y. On it, centred x 28.5, y 0, long side along y: a filled 2.25 lb oblong aluminium foil take-out pan (Choice 612LOB225LBC: 222 x 156 mm over the rim, 43 mm deep, sloped walls) with 400 g cooked rice, 425 g in all. Rim: a flat flange about 9 mm wide with its outer 8 mm lip turned straight up all round; corners cut at 45 deg (12 mm). On the flange lies the pan's foil-laminated board lid (213 x 152 mm, corners rounded), white side up, its edge 1.5 mm inside the lip. The lip is marked into 24 sections for scoring: 6 per long side (32 mm), 4 per short side (33 mm), one per cut corner (17 mm).
scoring: Measured at the end with a ruler. A lip section is folded when its free edge lies within 1.4 mm of the lid (within 10 deg of flat). Score 0 if: the lid is off its seat (centre moved over 4 mm, raised over 2 mm, or tilted over 3 deg relative to the pan); the pan is tipped over 10 deg, off the board, or crushed (under 40 mm tall); a gripper centre is within 10 cm of the lid (not let go and moved clear); or under 25% of the rim length is folded. Else 0.25: some side under 50% folded; 0.5: every side at least 50% folded (lid caught on all four sides); 0.75: at least 90% of the rim length folded; 1.0: all 24 sections folded.
reset_notes: Use a new pan and lid for each trial (a crimped rim can't be reset). Fill the pan with 400 g cooked rice, lay the lid on the flange white side up, turn the lip's outer 8 mm straight up all round against a ruler edge, mark the 24 sections, and set the pan on the board at its taped outline.
fidelity: The rim lip is 24 rigid foil sections (32 mm on the sides, 17 mm at the cut corners), each hinged to the pan at the lid edge and held wherever it is bent by joint friction equal to its yield moment (0.25 N·m per m of rim, about 1 N at the lip edge; corners twice that): plastic folding with no springback. Foil does not stretch or pleat between sections. Pan walls are rigid (no denting), the rice is only pan mass, and the lid is a rigid 1.5 mm board.
